title: Accuracy and Repeatability Targets
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robot Arm Anatomy
description: Classify four sets of five landing points on a target as accurate, repeatable, both or neither, then see the mean point and the spread that decide the answer. Used in Chapter 2.

educational.topic: Accuracy and repeatability of a robot arm
learningObjectives: Classify four sets of landing points as accurate or not and repeatable or not, using a stated distance threshold, with at least 3 of 4 sets classified correctly on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Show the five points on a target beside their offsets and ask for a two-part decision (centered? tight?), then reveal the mean and the spread that settle it
keyQuestions: Is the group of points centered on the target?
Which of the two problems can calibration fix?
commonMisconceptions: A repeatable arm is also an accurate one
If the average is on target the arm is precise
Accuracy and repeatability are two names for the same spec
assessmentOpportunities: Four committed labels, one attempt each; 3 of 4 for mastery

controls.label: Check / Next set / See score / Try again
